correctness.rationale: The additive function F(n)=∑_{p^a∥n} log[(p^a+1)/(∑_{d|a}p^d)] has a limiting law by the Erdős–Wintner conditions; the Lévy continuity criterion applies because f(p)=log(1+1/p)≠0 for all primes and ∑1/p diverges, so δ=P(X>0). For p>31 all exponents a≥2 satisfy local ratio <1, so a=1 upper-majorizes positive-exponent states. Integer upper logarithm grids β=50001/50000 preserve strict event inclusion; 11 capped small primes have explicitly charged missing mass. An independently rerun integer-convolution certificate over 168 primes ≤1000 generated 153387 coefficients, offset −52491 and threshold 51991; exact rational comparison gives P(S≥−500)<784271/10^6 and omitted mass <145/10^6. Infinite tail U=∑_{p>1000}1_{E_p>0}/p has E exp(1000U)<6, so Markov and rational exp bounds give P(U>500logβ)<300/10^6. Total strict upper <784716/10^6. The finite certificate and analytic infinite-tail argument are separate; no numerical finite-n density extrapolation.
